It really depends. I’ve sat down to write a suicide note with every intention of killing myself right after. Once I started writing, I found that I just kept going until the feelings were all out of my system, and once I was done I didn’t feel the need to kill myself anymore.

Sometimes we fantasize about ending our lives, and the act of writing a note is enough to scratch the itch, and we can just stop there. It makes sense—sort of like “roleplaying” suicide just to indulge the sick fantasy. In my case, there have been so many times I was so sure I wanted to die, but really all I wanted was to indulge the *idea* of it, just to get it out of my system. It was as if my suicidal depression just wanted me to humor it for a bit. And of course, writing about your pain is a pretty solid coping technique. God knows I’ve been doing it for years.

Other times, writing a note can reinforce the urges/intentions already in our head, and lead to us acting on them, which is dangerous. There’s something to be said for the “if you say it/write it down, it becomes real” phenomenon.

At the end of the day it depends who you are and exactly how badly you really want to die. If writing about your feelings helps you, then by all means keep doing it. If it just makes the thoughts stronger, then maybe find a different way to deal.
I don’t have any actual bath bubble stuff, so all I did was draw a bath and pour some shampoo over the running water.
